blocks.content: Article 32 is an integral part of the basic structure of the Constitution and is the very heart and soul of it.

rows: Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights

items: High Courts (Article 226) have a broader writ jurisdiction than the Supreme Court (Article 32) because High Courts can issue writs for ordinary legal rights in addition to Fundamental Rights.
Certiorari is both preventive and curative in nature, whereas Prohibition is purely preventive.
The Supreme Court cannot refuse to exercise its writ jurisdiction under Article 32 because seeking remedy under Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and is itself a Fundamental Right.
The five types of writs are Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo-Warranto.
Habeas Corpus is the only writ that can be issued against both public authorities and private individuals.
Mandamus cannot be issued against private individuals, the President of India, or State Governors.
Quo-Warranto can be petitioned by any interested person, not necessarily only the aggrieved party.
